title: Elgar's band and Darnell's jazz violin at Navy Pier
summary: Levy goes nightly to Navy Pier to hear Darnell's strong jazz violin with Elgar's band and attends a jazz concert featuring Cliff King and Darnell.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Did you get to know the musicians around town at that time?
Well, yes, I knew Charlie Ogden and his whole band, Darnell, Joe Suttler, and the whole band.

They were at Harmon's Dremlin. Yeah, and they also played on the Navy Pier. Yes. They played the Navy Pier. You hear them? Yes. Went to the Pier every night because Darnell played such a terrific violin, and he played so strong, you could hear the violin with the band. Other violin players, you couldn't hear them when the band was playing. And then he played all those extra notes that we were enthused over hearing, and I just made it my business to him. And Darnell was young. I think he's a year younger than I am. And then Elgus Oxler gave a concert at Oxler Hall, a jazz concert. I think one of the first I ever heard about. He told me about it. Yes. He gave him. And they featured Darnell playing the jazz violin. Cliff King played the jazz clarinet solo. And Joe Sutler was featured. They played Tiger Rag and played umpteen choruses, and everybody had a ball. They played it. It was terrific. And during intermission, I went down. Well, after I went down. I think either intermission or after it was over, I went backstage, talked to see Darnell. And Darnell had a clarinet. I said, do you want to play clarinet, Darnell? He said, yes. He said, gee whiz. Everybody thinks Cliff King is the greatest in the world. He said, I can learn how to play that clarinet. And he played a few notes. He said, see I'm doing it. See the finger. And see, you got to pull all your fingers down. That's when I first had my first music talk with Darnell. But he was always my idol because he played such terrific things. And it looked like he played it so easy. And the rest of us kids, we were studying. We just couldn't do it. And Darnell had so much talent. That's what it was. He had so much talent. An inborn ear for broken cords or the notes that would pass over the cords.
